Evaluation is based on one interview.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: "I leaned harder on the contractor's numbers. The peer projects weren't identical — different vendors, different corridor layouts — so the comparison felt soft. We went with 24 months."
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Baseline schedule selection contains the hidden planning-forecasting instance: the PM favors best-case contractor productivity and discounts the available peer duration range.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: "Field crews verify positions as a matter of course before they dig in any segment, so it felt like that tolerance note was already covered by standard practice."
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The post-survey resource-allocation reasoning contains Illusion of Control, while the later reflection that the conflict was obvious contains Hindsight Bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: "Those numbers weren't something I wanted to sit with heading into board season, honestly — reviewing and pushing that forward before the next monitoring cycle gave us anything better felt premature."
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Handling of the quantified contractor risk report contains the hidden information-avoidance/Ostrich Effect instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: "We couldn't afford to lose $4 million that was already ours. That was the deciding factor, even though the engineering lead's case for the full protocol was solid."
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The final testing choice contains the explicit loss-versus-equivalent-gain framing that defines the hidden Loss Aversion/Loss Framing instance.

instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG finding fully describes treating routine verification as sufficient control over an explicitly quantified residual uncertainty.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted tolerance-zone reasoning is accurately localized and represented, but the taxonomy label is wrong for the strict scorecard.

instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The evidence and behavioral consequences are accurately represented.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, all four positive reasoning segments are detected.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: Three of five hidden instances match at high_and_moderate; the remaining strict errors are the missed low-confidence hindsight instance and the normalcy-bias label substitution.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Four of five hidden instances match at high_and_moderate and all five match when low-confidence identified findings are included.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidates were supplied, so the candidate tier adds no information.
main_failure_modes: Normalcy bias was used instead of the hidden Illusion of Control label.
Hindsight Bias was assigned low confidence and is missed at the recommended threshold.
main_strengths: All findings are correctly localized to the supplied reasoning segments.
Mechanisms and quotations are generally faithful to the interview.
The planning fallacy, information avoidance/Ostrich Effect, and loss aversion findings are well supported.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The run has perfect segment-level coverage at the recommended threshold and strong mechanism-level performance, with a narrow taxonomy error and a conservative confidence assignment as the main limitations.
